subject: Fraud & Scams
title: Skimming: The Invisible Card Trap
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Skimming: The Invisible Card Trap.

hook.text: You swipe your card at a gas pump. A hidden device copies your card data in milliseconds.

buildup.text: Skimmers are small devices installed over real card readers at ATMs, gas pumps, and stores.

discovery.text: Modern skimmers are paper-thin and nearly invisible. Some use Bluetooth to send data wirelessly.

twist.text: Criminals can collect hundreds of card numbers from a single skimmer before anyone notices.

climax.text: Chip cards reduced skimming, but criminals adapted with shimming — targeting the chip reader itself.

punchline.text: The machine you trust with your card might be betraying you.

quiz.question: What is a card skimmer?
options: A hidden device that copies card data from readers
